key_insight: DLLM decoding wastes most compute because only a small subset of tokens is decodable at each diffusion step; attention-derived token importance strongly predicts which tokens are decodable, enabling targeted compute.
problem_solved: High decoding cost and compute inefficiency in Diffusion Large Language Models caused by parallel computation over token blocks where most tokens at each step are non-decodable and therefore wasteful.
method: Extract token-wise importance signals from attention to predict decodability per diffusion step.
Dynamically select and prioritize decodable tokens for full decoding work while applying lightweight updates to others.
Deploy FOCUS scheduling to adaptively allocate compute within token blocks, maintaining output quality with much less wasted computation.
impact: Reduces wasted compute and decoding latency for DLLMs, making diffusion-based LLMs more practical and cost-effective to deploy and scale without sacrificing generation quality.
visual_elements: Before vs After schematic: token-block compute heatmap showing wasted compute in baseline vs concentrated compute in FOCUS.
Attention heatmap over tokens aligned with a marker for 'decodable' tokens to illustrate the correlation.
Bar chart comparing compute/time (or FLOPs) and decoding latency: baseline vs FOCUS.
Flowchart of the FOCUS loop: attention → importance scoring → token selection → prioritized decoding.
paper_title: FOCUS: DLLMs Know How to Tame Their Compute Bound
paper_authors: Kaihua Liang, Xin Tan, An Zhong, Hong Xu, Marco Canini
